wire.headline: Energy firm reports profit drop and plans job cuts
sentences: The company's revenue increased by 7% year on year to reach 4.26bn GBP for the quarter ending 30 September.
Pre-tax profit declined by 12% to stand at 310m GBP.
The firm announced 850 job cuts, which represents about 6% of its workforce.
Two gas plants are scheduled to close by March 2027, with one located in Wales and the other in Kent.
CEO Marian Holt stated that the cost pressure has been sharper than expected.
Ofgem has opened an investigation into the company's billing system.
The dividend was held at 12.4p a share.
Shares fell by 4.2% during morning trading.

An analyst at Kestrel Securities stated that the planned job cuts will result in annual savings of 90m GBP.

ND.headline: UK energy firm announces 850 job cuts and reports 12% drop in pre-tax profit

sentences.text: The company reported a pre-tax profit decline of 12% to 310m GBP.
Plans include 850 job cuts which represent about 6% of the workforce.
An analyst from Kestrel Securities stated that the job cuts will save 90m GBP a year.
The trade union Unite intends to ballot its members on taking industrial action.
The Kent plant employs 410 staff and the local supply chain is exposed.
The MP for Deeside has requested an urgent meeting with the company.
Since 2024, 1,200 staff have left under a voluntary scheme.
Ofgem is scheduled to report preliminary findings by the end of 2026.
Shares closed at 268p, down 11p.
A customer group logged 3,400 billing complaints in six months.
Talks with unions are set to start on 4 November.
Ofgem fined the company 1.8m GBP in 2023 over billing issues.
The company stated there will be no compulsory redundancies before January 2027.
Kestrel Securities cut its price target to 240p from 290p.
The company employs 4,800 staff in the UK.
